# Cache continuation state and restore it after application readiness

## Platform difference

OH continuation callbacks and incoming state operate on the native lifecycle, which may precede application services and routing readiness.

## Implementation

Pica Comic removes premature startup route injection and changes onContinue from an async implementation to a synchronous callback using cached reader state. Venera waits for comic-source initialization before restoration, limits continuation to an active reader, updates mission state and clears stale cached state when the reader closes.

## Applicability

Transfer a serializable application snapshot with an explicit active/valid state. These projects integrate native continuation; availability still depends on the target product, API and devices.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Do not reconstruct required state through late asynchronous calls inside a callback expecting an immediate result. Inactive/stale payloads must be rejected. A channel and manifest are not proof of successful cross-device transfer.

## Verification

Test active and inactive readers, cold receiver startup, delayed content-source setup, invalid/missing source definitions, cancellation and state changes during a transfer.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
